findings.issue: `id` is set to `https://chorus4ai.org/`, the project website URL, which is also used verbatim as `page`. The bundle supplies no persistent identifier for the dataset itself. Using the landing page URL as the dataset identifier makes `id` and `page` indistinguishable and asserts an identity the bundle does not state. A traceable alternative attested by the bundle is the award identifier (OT2OD032701) or a project-scoped URI; at minimum the collision with `page` should be resolved.

Slot value asserts imaging de-identification as an applied method. The bundle (cohort_2_webinar) states only that 1000 images are available 'with de-id in process for larger cohort' — de-identification is in progress for the larger cohort, not completed. The parenthetical hedge is present but the value still lists it among methods applied to the dataset.

Boolean `true` is populated by inference from the presence of PICU and NICU admissions; the record's own `source_caveats` states 'The inclusion of minors is inferred'. Under the evidence boundary a boolean assertion about at-risk-population inclusion must be stated by the bundle, not derived. No source in the bundle characterizes the cohort as including at-risk populations. Either omit the object or drop the boolean and retain only the caveat.

Boolean `true` is not stated by any source. The bundle describes retrospective clinical data collection, an ethics pillar, and a legal framework, but no source makes a human-subjects-research determination; the record's own `source_caveats` concedes no determination is reported. Asserting the boolean converts an inference into a claim.

The instance entry 'De-identified radiology image available in the enclave' with counts 1000 carries a `source_caveats` describing a conflict between 1000 images (tier 4) and 7,642 admissions (tier 2). The caveat correctly notes these count different units, so there is no actual disagreement to record; the caveat as written implies a source conflict that the bundle does not contain. Reword to state the two figures measure different units without framing them as irreconcilable sources.

Only one Creator object is emitted, for Eric S. Rosenthal. The bundle (cohort_2_webinar) explicitly names a 'Bridge2AI CHoRUS Leadership Team' of six with affiliations: Eric Rosenthal (Massachusetts General Hospital), Azra Bihorac (University of Florida), Xiaoqian Jiang (UTHealth Houston), Yulia Strekalova (University of Florida), Parisa Rashidi (University of Florida), Manlik Kwong (Tufts University). The multivalued-slot rule requires one object per distinct entity; these five are relegated to `description` prose instead. `principal_investigator` need only be set on the Rosenthal entry.

Three of the four Maintainer objects place a person's name, role, organization and email entirely inside the free-text `maintainer_details` field while the declared `role` field is left empty on all four. The class declares `role` with an enum (data_subject, third_party, researcher, industry, academic_institution, government_agency, commercial_entity, non_profit_organization, crowdsourced, automated_system, other); `academic_institution` fits the CHoRUS/MGH contacts. Structure the declared field rather than restating in prose.

`role` on DataCollector is a plain string in this class (no enum declared), so 'data contributing site' and 'site data manager' are shape-conformant. However `maintainers[*].role` is enum-constrained and left unpopulated — flagged separately. No defect here; recorded for contrast to prevent an erroneous enum being added to DataCollector during repair.

Omitted although the bundle supports it. The cohort_2_webinar states access is conditioned on signing a licensing agreement and on institutional ('.edu') email, and eligibility is restricted to specified organization types; `ethics_approval_required` is not attested, but `institution_specific` or `project_specific` is directly supported by the '.edu' email requirement and program-scoped provisioning. At minimum the omission should be justified in `source_caveats` rather than left silent.

Omitted. The bundle does not state a HIPAA compliance determination for the dataset, so omission is defensible under the evidence boundary; however the AI-LEARN curriculum item names 'HIPAA/GDPR compliance for OMOP/FHIR data' as a training topic, which is a statement about coursework and not about this dataset. Confirm no value is added on the strength of that line — populating from it would be an unsupported claim.

`start_date` and `end_date` are declared `date`-ranged fields on CollectionTimeframe and are left empty while the award period (2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30) is written into `timeframe_details` prose. The award period is the project period, not the data collection period, so it should not be written into `start_date`/`end_date`; but the current object then carries no structured value at all. Consider whether the object earns its place or whether the award dates belong only in funders/notes.

`status` is declared `string` and its description gives examples of controlled vocabulary-like values (draft, published, deprecated). The value here is a full sentence ('Initial dataset released under controlled access; data acquisition and modality expansion ongoing.'), which is descriptive prose rather than a status token. The substance duplicates `updates.update_details`.

Includes `OTHER` without any indication of which standard `OTHER` denotes. The bundle names EDF+, Persyst and the OHNLP open source schema as the standards not covered by the enum; `conforms_to` does record them in prose, so the pairing is traceable, but a single `OTHER` collapses three distinct unlisted standards into one term. Acceptable but imprecise.

`grants` is a declared field of range Grant[] on FundingMechanism and is left empty while the award number OT2OD032701, project number 1OT2OD032701-01, application ID 10472824, award amount 5880300 and project period are all written into the free-text `notes`. The declared structured field should carry the grant identifier.
Omitted. Correct — the bundle supplies no DOI for the dataset. Recorded to confirm the omission is deliberate and not an oversight.

Omitted while the bundle states '23 Tb Waveform data' and '1.6 Billion Rows of EHR OMOP data'. The waveform figure is a size but is stated for one modality only and in ambiguous units (Tb), and no total across all collections is given, so omission of `total_size_bytes` is defensible. Recorded so the reconciliation states the reasoning rather than leaving it silent.

Omitted. The bundle states a 'Working command of English' requirement for training-program applicants, which is a fact about applicants and not about the dataset's content language. Omission is correct; recorded to guard against populating it from that line during repair.

The email 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' is transcribed verbatim from the website, which is correct, and the misspelling is flagged in an adjacent `source_caveats`. This is the right handling; recorded to prevent a well-meaning 'correction' to harvard.edu during repair, which would fabricate an address the bundle does not contain.

The description carries the leadership-team roster ('Eric Rosenthal (Massachusetts General Hospital), Azra Bihorac, Yulia Strekalova, and Parisa Rashidi (University of Florida)...'), which is content the `creators` slot declares fields for. Once `creators` is expanded per the finding above, this sentence should be removed from `description` rather than duplicated in both places.

Omitted. Correct, since the dataset spans tabular OMOP data, DICOM imaging, waveforms and tokenized text, so no single boolean is true of it. Recorded to confirm the omission is judged rather than overlooked.

summary: Nineteen findings against the full record. Four are high severity: `id` reuses the project landing-page URL and collides with `page`, giving the dataset no distinct identifier; and three boolean/method assertions — imaging de-identification as an applied method, `at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included`, and `human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects` — convert inference into claim, each already conceded as inferred or unreported in its own adjacent caveat. Seven medium findings concern structure rather than truth: `creators` collapses a six-person leadership team the bundle names explicitly into one object with the rest demoted to `description` prose; `maintainers` leaves the enum-constrained `role` field empty on every object while packing name, organization and email into free text; `funders[0].grants` is empty while the grant identifiers sit in `notes`; `collection_timeframes[0]` carries no structured date at all; and `license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission` is omitted despite an attested institution-specific access condition. One medium finding notes that the instances[3] caveat frames a units mismatch as a source conflict. The remaining low findings are precision and hygiene items, several recorded specifically to confirm that a deliberate omission (`doi`, `language`, `is_tabular`, `total_size_bytes`) or a deliberate verbatim transcription (the misspelled maintainer email) is not disturbed during repair. No slot value was found that the bundle contradicts outright, and no enum value outside the schema's declared sets was emitted; the record's tier-based handling of the 50,000 versus 45K admissions disagreement is correct as written.
